code: killer_check("greatest_hits") #> <killer_check> greatest_hits (qualitative)  #>   colours: 11  #>   worst-case CIEDE2000 separation by vision type: #>     normal    14.6 #>     deutan    13.3 #>     protan    12.7 #>     tritan    12.5 #>   contrast vs white: 1.52 - 10.08 #>   contrast vs black: 2.08 - 13.80 #>   lightness (L*):    27.9 - 83.9 #>   monotone lightness: FALSE killer_cvd_grid("greatest_hits") rb <- grDevices::rainbow(8) op <- par(mar = c(0.5, 5.5, 1.5, 0.5)) plot(c(0, 8), c(0, 2), type = "n", axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "",      main = "rainbow(8)") rect(0:7, 1.1, 1:8, 1.9, col = rb, border = NA) rect(0:7, 0.1, 1:8, 0.9, col = killer_cvd(rb, "deutan"), border = NA) text(c(-0.2, -0.2), c(1.5, 0.5), c("normal", "deutan"), adj = 1, xpd = NA) par(op)  min(killer_check(colours = rb)$min_distance) #> [1] 0.9610308 worst <- vapply(killer_names(), function(nm) {   min(killer_check(nm)$min_distance) }, numeric(1)) round(sort(worst), 1) #> greatest_hits     the_works     hot_space all_that_jazz         flash  #>          12.5          16.0          16.2          16.8          17.3  #>  mirror_queen       miracle       game_on kind_of_magic        regina  #>          17.4          17.6          17.8          17.8          18.0  #>    robot_news      heavenly  heart_attack   opera_night      race_day  #>          18.1          18.4          18.4          19.1          20.3  #>      innuendo  #>          21.1

title: Queen album palette scales for ggplot2 — scale_killer
text: palette Palette name, e.g. "flash". See killer_names(). type Palette type draw . Discrete scales default "qualitative"; continuous binned scales default "sequential" accept "diverging" data meaningful midpoint. direction 1 palette's natural order, -1 reverse . ... Passed ggplot2::discrete_scale(), ggplot2::continuous_scale() ggplot2::binned_scale(). aesthetics Character string vector aesthetics apply scale . Useful e.g. c("colour", "fill"). na.value Colour missing values. guide Guide use. See ggplot2::guides().

title: Queen album palette scales for ggplot2 — scale_killer
text: ggplot2 scale, added plot +.

title: Queen album palette scales for ggplot2 — scale_killer
text: suffix follows ggplot2 convention: _d discrete - one colour per category, palette's qualitative colours. _c continuous - smooth gradient, interpolated CIELAB. _b binned - continuous variable cut bins. scale_color_* spellings provided aliases every scale_colour_*.

title: Queen album palette scales for ggplot2 — scale_killer
code: library(ggplot2)  # Discrete / qualitative ggplot(mpg, aes(displ, hwy, colour = class)) +   geom_point() +   scale_colour_killer_d("greatest_hits")   # Continuous / sequential ggplot(faithfuld, aes(waiting, eruptions, fill = density)) +   geom_raster() +   scale_fill_killer_c("heavenly")   # Continuous / diverging, centred on zero df <- data.frame(x = 1:20, y = 1:20, z = seq(-5, 5, length.out = 20)) ggplot(df, aes(x, y, colour = z)) +   geom_point(size = 4) +   scale_colour_killer_c("innuendo", type = "diverging",                         limits = c(-5, 5))   # Binned ggplot(faithfuld, aes(waiting, eruptions, fill = density)) +   geom_raster() +   scale_fill_killer_b("flash")

title: killerPals 0.1.0
text: First release. 48 palettes: qualitative, sequential diverging palette Queen’s fifteen studio albums, plus greatest_hits family drawn whole catalogue. Palettes derived album covers data-raw/build_palettes.py, optimises one worst-case CIEDE2000 separation simulated deuteranopic, protanopic tritanopic vision, subject WCAG contrast lightness constraints. killer_pal() killer_pal_fun() get colours; killer_names() killer_palette_info() browse . ggplot2 scales discrete (_d), continuous (_c) binned (_b) aesthetics, scale_colour_* / scale_fill_* form scale_color_* aliases. Accessibility tooling: killer_check(), killer_cvd(), killer_cvd_grid(), killer_distance(), killer_distance_matrix(), killer_contrast() killer_luminance() — work arbitrary colours, just package’s.
